title: How random forests work
prompt: Explain how a typical random forest trains its trees and combines their predictions. Use either classification or regression for your example.
objective: Describe random forest training and how the individual predictions form a forest prediction.
expected_scope: Cover row sampling, feature sampling and prediction aggregation for one task.
hint: Think about what changes between trees and what changes between splits.
reference_explanation: In a standard bootstrap forest, each tree learns from a sample of training rows drawn with replacement. At each split, the algorithm considers a random subset of features. The forest combines the trees’ outputs. For regression it averages their predictions. Classifiers can combine votes or class probabilities, depending on the implementation. For example, scikit-learn chooses the class with the highest mean tree probability.

criteria.description: Describes drawing training rows with replacement for individual trees.
Describes selecting candidate features randomly at each split.
Describes a valid prediction aggregation for the chosen task.

critical_misconceptions: Saying each tree is trained to correct the previous tree’s mistakes.

sources.title: Leo Breiman — Random Forests, sections 1–2 and 4
